intro.title: Redux Toolkit — createSlice & createAsyncThunk
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that manages a list of posts fetched from a mock API. You'll learn how to use Redux Toolkit's createSlice to define a slice of state with reducers for synchronous actions, and createAsyncThunk to handle asynchronous data fetching. The core programming concept is state management using Redux patterns within Vue, focusing on predictable updates and side-effect handling. You'll work with Vuex for Vue integration, JavaScript async/await, and Redux Toolkit utilities. By the end, you'll understand how to structure state, dispatch actions, and manage loading and error states in a beginner-friendly way.
intro.usecase: In real applications, createSlice and createAsyncThunk are essential for managing complex state in data-driven interfaces like e-commerce dashboards, social media feeds, or admin panels. For example, when building a product management dashboard, you'd use createSlice to handle local UI state (like filters or pagination) while createAsyncThunk manages asynchronous operations such as fetching product data, updating inventory, or processing orders. This pattern keeps your code organized when dealing with loading states, errors, and success updates across multiple API calls. Developers implement this daily in scenarios like user authentication flows, real-time notifications, or any interface requiring consistent state management during data fetching and updates.

objectives: Implement a Redux Toolkit slice using createSlice to define state and reducers
Configure asynchronous actions with createAsyncThunk for API data fetching
Initialize and integrate the Redux store with Vue components using Vuex or Pinia patterns
Manipulate component state by dispatching synchronous actions from the slice
Update UI elements to reflect loading, success, and error states from async thunks
Bind component data to Redux state selectors for reactive rendering
Construct a complete feature module with slice, thunks, and component integration

steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind each button to its corresponding method. Place the buttons inside the template section of your component.
